::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Confusion regarding a step to solve a limit using Squeeze Theorem.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4753532/confusion-regarding-a-step-to-solve-a-limit-using-squeeze-theorem), asked by [Anthony](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/1209276/anthony) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2023-08-15; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I am trying to find the following limit using the Squeeze Theorem:
>
> $$\lim_{x\to0^+} \sqrt[3]x\left(3-\sin^2\left(\frac\pi x\right)\right)$$
> I began by writing down the range of $\sin:$
> $$-1\leq\sin{x}\leq1$$
>
> But here is where I'm confused, since it is $\sin^2x$ in the original limit, is the next step to square all three parts of the inequality? Or, do you begin with the range of $\sin^2x$?
:::

You can only “square all three parts of an inequality” if the parts are nonnegative. Instead, observe that
$$-1 \leq \sin z \leq 1 \iff 0 \leq |\sin z| \leq 1$$
This means that
$$0 \leq |\sin z|^2 \leq 1$$
Since $|\sin z|^2 = |\sin^2 z| = \sin^2 z$, you have that $0 \leq \sin^2 z \leq 1$.
